headline: Floor Boss carts now duck and pass — the jam-up that capped every floor is gone
lede: Autopilot floors froze at the arms: a cart nose-blocked by a rival for longer than one round could not nudge past it, and the whole depot waited for the jam law's 160-tick timeout. Carts now read a rival's facing, slip into the empty arm bay beside it, and resume the instant the route opens — the depot flows, the floors score higher, and self-inflicted freezes still answer to the jam law exactly as before.

notes.text: Yield delay swept 4/6/8/12 ticks before picking a number: 12 fires zero (autopilot repaths past shallower blocks — the freeze is the no-route stall, not the blocked step), 4 wins 14/15 seeds, autopilot average 1425 vs 1420, freezes 0, seed 42's late jam recovers 1323→1408. A cart waiting on a rival can only cost time — the law is a floor-score floor, not a ceiling.

Ducks are perpendicular only — pulling off along the route would cost the cart its place, so a corridor between two rivals still paces. Swept volumes through corners remain faked by the jam clock; that gap stays open in the README, now worded as what the courtesy covers.

Ducks cost 14 energy — a courtesy is never free — and the ducking cart paints a cyan traffic ring so you can read which cart is giving way. The arm-bay crush at (16,3) that this whole pass is named for: watch it live on jalfern.com/retrogames/floor-boss.

324 sim gates (+17), a hand-mutant (duck stubbed to a no-op) killed by two named gates, per-bot Y and tally DK marks joined into the state hash per the state-hash law, and two new browser legs — a cyan-pixel ring check and a staged duel where a nose-blocked rig proves it leaves the bay in 11 ticks and carries its ring while holding.
